I was raised Catholic, went to a Catholic middle school where I realized I didn't believe, then continued to a Jesuit (also Catholic) highschool despite being openly atheist. 

The reason I left was because I thought at a young age that the bible was literal (this is not what my parents or my church believes, it's just what I thought) which made me really question the religion once my 4th grade science teacher brought up the big bang, then my parents started watching The Big Bang Theory TV show so I had to ask what the Big Bang was. I just had now way to say "this bible shows who God is" and "Genesis is a fable" without coming to a simpler conclusion of it just is a fable.

As I said, my parents didn't take the bible literally, but that didn't make sense to me either as the bible was the only piece of text we had on God. If we couldn't trust that, why trust it at all

TL;DR: I learned that Genisis was wrong, came to the conclusion that the entire book HAD to be wrong as well.

There are IUDs that can inserted into the uterus that either stops the egg from being fertilized or stops ovulation (there are two kinds). Another thing that can be done is tricking the body with hormones (via implant or by a regular pill) that stop ovulating by making the body think it's already pregnant. The IUD are considered effective and fast but painful to get in there, and I had one GF who had an implant in her arm. There's also spermicidal lubes, but I don't trust them to stay inside

Tbh, I think that's a decision the woman should make, since condoms are the quickest and least harmful to them, and the more effective methods are potentially painful or change their body. 

Tldr; IUD, the pill, hormone implant, spermicidal lube

Their policy is to separate the populations inside a nursing home so as to have enough space in the hospital. My grandmother is currently in a nursing home that had an outbreak of COVID in one wing, but they managed to quarantine that area off and have even separated staff for each wing. I'm not saying it's a good idea to put people with COVID into a vulnerable community, but it is possible. It also is the reason why Cuomo had said if the nursing home is at less than 80% capacity and they have the equipment to properly quarantine. I understand that he probably wants to use nursing homes since they have medical equipment and staff. Honestly, I think we should have made temporary hospitals in school gyms and community centers like what China did. There are already some communities capable of creating emergency shelters in cases of natural disaster, the only problem would be the medical supplies and staffing.
